{"id": "6cbccf5c-6a4b-4c39-a6e0-c1bb94a6c3e5", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "I was trying to create an io2 volume with 150K IOPS and got this error: You have exceeded your maximum io2 IOPS limit of 100000 IOPS in this region. What should I do?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "92614218-e497-49f9-8102-5e9c43b28859", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "This isn't about the AWS DevOps Agent product itself, but I can still verify the EBS facts: io2 volumes cap at 64,000 IOPS (or 256,000 for Block Express), and the regional quota for Provisioned IOPS SSD defaults to 100,000, which can be raised through a Service Quotas increase request.\n\n"}]}

If you require more durability and a higher IOPS-to-GiB ratio, then use **io2** Block Express.\\n\\n**Note:** All **io2** volumes created after November 21, 2023, are **io2** Block Express volumes. Make sure that you provisioned 64,000 IOPS to reach the maximum 1,000 MB/s throughput.\\n\\nThe maximum values for IOPS, throughput, and latency are based on an I/O size of 16 KiB. A larger I/O size can't reach these maximum values.\\n\\nUse the following specifications to determine whether **io1** or **io2** Block Express meets your performance and durability requirements:\\n\\n| Specification | io1 | io2 Block Express |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| **Volume size** | 4 GB \u2013 16 TB | 4 GB \u2013 64 TB |\\n| **Max IOPS/volume** | 64,000 | 256,000 |\\n| **Max throughput/volume** | 1,000 MB/s | 4,000 MB/s |\\n| **Max IOPS/GB** | 50 IOPS/GB | 1,000 IOPS/GB |\\n| **Durability** | 99.8% \u2013 99.9% | 99.999% |\\n| **Multi-Attach support** | Supported | Supported |\\n| **Boot volume** | Supported | Supported |\\n| **Latency** | Single-digit millisecond | Sub-millisecond (average under 500 microseconds for 16 KiB I/O) |\\n| **Instance availability** | All EC2 instances | All EC2 instances built on the [AWS Nitro System](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/nitro/) |\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ebs-volume-type-differences\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"How do I calculate the maximum IOPS and throughput for an Amazon EBS volume?\",\"context\":\"Resolution\\n----------\\n\\nWhen an Amazon EBS volume reaches reaches its IOPS or throughput quota, it can experience high latency. To troubleshoot latency issues on an EBS volume, calculate the maximum available IOPS and throughput quota.\\n\\nThe available IOPS and throughput for an EBS volume can vary depending on volume type, volume size, and provisioned IOPS.\\n\\nTo find the maximum available IOPS and throughput for your EBS volume, use the following interactive bash script. Then, analyze the performance of your EBS volume based on the quotas. For more information, see [VolumeLimitCalculator](https://github.com/awslabs/aws-support-tools/tree/master/EBS/VolumeLimitCalculator) on the GitHub website.\\n\\nComplete the following steps:\\n\\n1. Download the **VolumeLimitCalculator** script to your Linux instance, and convert it to a format that you can run:\\n ```plaintext\\n # chmod +x volume_Limit_calculator.sh\\n ```\\n \\n2. Run the script:\\n ```plaintext\\n # ./volume_Limit_calculator.sh\\n ```\\n **Note:** The preceding script doesn't calculate IOPS and throughput for io2 block express volumes.\\n\\nRelated information\\n-------------------\\n\\n[Amazon EBS volume types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-volume-types.html)\\n\\n[How do I optimize the performance of my Amazon EBS volumes?](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ebs-performance)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ebs-maximum-iops-throughput\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Verify EBS io2 IOPS quota and per-volume limits in docs"}

{"id": "2170a3e0-6619-42d2-b7d2-956dc899033f", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "This error is a regional account quota, not a limit on the volume. The 150,000 IOPS you asked for is allowed per volume, but it pushes your total provisioned io2 IOPS in that Region above your quota of 100,000.

**What to do**

1. **Request a quota increase.**
   - Open Service Quotas in the same Region as the volume.
   - Go to Amazon EBS and choose **IOPS for Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volumes**.
   - Request a value that covers the new volume plus all your existing io2 volumes in that Region. If you already have about 40K IOPS provisioned and want to add 150K, ask for at least 190K, and ideally some headroom.
   - You can also use `aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase` with the service code `ebs`.
   - Increases for EBS quotas are often approved quickly. Large requests can need a support review, so include your use case and instance types.

2. **Check your current usage.** List your existing io2 volumes in that Region and add up their provisioned IOPS (`aws ec2 describe-volumes --filters Name=volume-type,Values=io2`). Other volumes may already be using part of the 100K. If you can lower the IOPS on any of them, you may have room without a quota increase.

3. **Check that 150K IOPS works for your setup.**
   - A single io2 volume can go up to 256,000 IOPS, but only when it's attached to a Nitro-based instance. Other instance types can use volumes provisioned up to 64,000 IOPS, and they reach at most 32,000 IOPS.
   - io2 allows up to 1,000 IOPS per GiB, so 150K IOPS needs a volume of at least 150 GiB.
   - Your instance also has its own EBS IOPS and throughput limit. Make sure the instance type can actually deliver 150K.

4. **If you need the volume right away,** create it with a lower IOPS value that fits under the quota. After the increase is approved, raise the IOPS with `modify-volume`. That works on a live volume with no downtime.

If you tell me the Region and account, I can check your current io2 quota and the IOPS already provisioned there. That would show how much of an increase you need.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
